Commentary.Commentary: The players and the umpires are back into the middle to start the second innings. Its Dawid Malan and Jonny Bairstow as the opening batters for England. Mustafizur Rahman to start the attack for Bangladesh. Lets Play!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

England's fast bowlers were the stars of the show, producing a brilliant performance. Reece Topley was exceptional, claiming a three-wicket haul for his skipper. Rashid Khan, the Afghan spin wizard, also made his presence felt by dismissing two Bangladeshi batters. Remarkably, England utilized the services of nine different bowlers in the innings, including six fast bowlers and three spinners, showcasing their bowling depth and versatility. As the action now shifts to England's innings, they face the challenge of chasing down the DLS revised target of 197 runs in 37 overs. Will they rise to the occasion, or can the Bangladeshi bowlers conjure a game-changing twist? The answer awaits in the upcoming second innings.

Tanzid Hasan and Mehidy Hasan emerged as the silver lining, conjuring a gritty partnership worth 52 runs. Just when it seemed they might steady the ship, Tanzid was dismissed by a breathtaking delivery from Mark Wood. From there on, it was mostly a solo effort from Mehidy, who valiantly battled on to score a commendable 74 off 89 balls. Unfortunately, the rest of the Bangladeshi batting lineup struggled to make an impact, with most batsmen failing to even breach the 20-run mark, leading to a significant middle-order collapse.

The first innings of this World Cup warm-up showdown between England and Bangladesh brought forth a riveting display of cricketing drama. After winning the toss, Bangladesh chose to set a target for the English side. However, their journey to a respectable total was fraught with difficulties, especially at the top of the order and they could only post a total of 188 losing 9 wickets in 37 overs. The Bangladeshi batsmen faced a fiery English bowling attack that claimed two quick wickets in the opening 10 overs.

Commentary.Commentary: The umpires and the players are back on the ground after the break. The play starts soon with Bangladesh to bat for 7 more overs. Mehidy Hasan and Towhid Hridoy walk in to take the place for Bangladesh and Gus Atkinson to start the proceedings for England. Lets Play!

UPDATE - 7.20 pm IST (1.50 PM GMT) - Finally some good news. The rain has stopped now and we have a restart time of 7.30 pm IST. It is going to be a 37-overs-per-side encounter, if there's no further rain. We expect to have the full 37 over game from here.

UPDATE - 7.09 pm IST (1.39 pm GMT) - The waiting game continues! It is still drizzling and the covers are firmly in place. All we can do right now is hope that the rain relents quickly and we can get to watch some cricket. Stick around for further updates.

UPDATE - 6.36 pm IST (1.06 pm GMT) - It's another bad news for the fans as the rain is back at the ACA Stadium and the covers are coming back on. Just when we were building up to start at 7.00 pm IST for a 40-over game, we have another halt at the start of play.

UPDATE - 5.49 pm IST (12.19 pm GMT) - It seems to have stopped raining and the covers are slowly being peeled off. The match officials have decided to have an inspection at 6.30 pm IST (1.00 pm GMT). Let's keep our fingers crossed and hope that the ground staff can get the field ready for the inspection. We will keep you posted.

UPDATE - 5.25 pm IST (11.55 am GMT) - It's still raining at the ACA Stadium and it does not look like it's going to stop for a while. We might be looking at a shortage in overs of play keeping in mind the time to dry the outfield once the rain stops. As we wait for the rain to abate, you can switch tabs and follow the other warm-up game taking place in Thiruvananthapuram between New Zealand and South Africa.

UPDATE - 4.50 pm IST (11.20 am GMT) - The covers are still in place and the ground looks bleak at the moment. We will get back to you with any major update but at this moment it looks like a long day ahead.

UPDATE - 4.24 pm IST (10.54 am GMT) - Oh, no! It has started to rain and the ground staff come rushing in with the covers. It had gotten gloomy in the past few overs and the clouds have opened up now. The skies do not paint a promising picture but let's hope that this is just a passing shower. Stay tuned for further updates.

Drinks break! England have continued to chip away with wickets but are yet to see the back of Mehidy Hasan. With spinners coming into play now, England will look to run through the lower order with spin. On the other hand, Mehidy Hasan looks unperturbed with the loss of wickets at the other end and holds the key for Bangladesh to post a respectable total.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the action to start. The sun is out as the two umpires and players make their way out to the middle. Tanzid Hasan and Litton Das will open the innings for Bangladesh. Reece Topley will start with the new ball for England. Here we go...

PITCH REPORT - Dinesh Karthik is pitchside. He says that this is the same surface that was to be used for the game between India and England. Mentions that there is enough covering of dry grass on the wicket. Feels that it will be good to bat in the second innings. Shares that there will not be much help for the spinners.

Jos Buttler, the captain of England, says that they would have bowled first. Adds that they want to give the bowlers a good run around. Mentions that there are a couple of guys who are still to be fit for the opening game. Feels that they are as ready as they can and they look forward to the event. Shares that they know what works well for the team.

Bangladesh's stand-in skipper Najmul Hossain Shanto says that they will bat first. Adds that they batted second in the last game and therefore, they want to bat first here. Informs that Shakib Al Hasan is fit and will be available for the first game. Mentions that they played good cricket in the last match and hopes that everyone can contribute. Reckons that this is the last opportunity to play good cricket befor the main event.

Bangladesh - Taskin Ahmed, Nasum Ahmed, Shakib Al Hasan (C), Litton Das (WK), Tanzid Hasan, Najmul Hossain Shanto, Towhid Hridoy, Mushfiqur Rahim, Mahmudullah, Mehidy Hasan, Mahedi Hasan, Mustafizur Rahman, Hasan Mahmud, Shoriful Islam, Tanzim Hasan Sakib.

England - Jonny Bairstow, Dawid Malan, Joe Root, Harry Brook, Jos Buttler (C/WK), Liam Livingstone, Moeen Ali, Sam Curran, David Willey, Adil Rashid, Gus Atkinson, Reece Topley, Mark Wood, Chris Woakes, Ben Stokes.
TOSS - The coin toss lands in the favour of Bangladesh and they have opted to BAT first.

On the flip side, Bangladesh's journey to this World Cup hasn't been paved with roses, particularly highlighted by their underwhelming performance in the Asia Cup. Their Achilles' heel has been the struggling top order, a concern they're keen to address. Yet, this is a team renowned for their resilience, capable of upsetting the biggest names on their day. With seasoned warriors like Shakib Al Hasan and Mushfiqur Rahim in their ranks, Bangladesh aims to script a tale worth remembering. Their quest for the coveted trophy begins here, and it's a formidable challenge they embrace with open arms. No matter the outcome, cricket enthusiasts are in for an electrifying spectacle as these cricketing giants collide. So, fasten your seatbelts, folks, as the action is about to erupt on your screens! Stay tuned for an unforgettable showdown! The toss coming up soon.

As we dive into this thrilling encounter, both teams stand poised and ready for the grand stage. These warm-up matches serve as the final dress rehearsals, allowing teams to fine-tune their strategies and adapt to the conditions that will shape the entire tournament. England, the defending champions and ODI juggernauts, arrive under the able leadership of the in-form Jos Buttler. With the return of the indomitable Ben Stokes from retirement, their batting lineup has a razor-sharp edge. Buttler, Stokes, and their comrades-in-arms pose a formidable challenge for any opponent. The English fast bowling brigade, featuring the likes of Mark Wood, Gus Atkinson, Sam Curran, and Reece Topley, has been firing on all cylinders, making England a force to be reckoned with.

Ladies and gentlemen, welcome to a cricketing spectacle that promises fireworks! It's the World Cup Warm-Up match, and today, we have England locking horns with Bangladesh at the vibrant ACA Stadium in Guwahati. While the current weather paints a sunny picture, our weather prophets predict a visit from the rain gods in the later stages of this contest, adding an extra layer of intrigue.
... MATCH DAY ...

The biggest cricketing event is on the horizon and in the final round of warm-up matches, England take on Bangladesh in Guwahati as both teams look to tighten the screws before the 2023 Cricket World Cup begins. England are the reigning champions and have a fantastic white-ball team but they will need to hit their stride as a slow start could be pretty challenging to bounce back from. Their previous warm-up game against India was washed out at the same venue, so they hope to get some game time under their belt. Bangladesh on the other hand put on a dominant display against Sri Lanka in their previous warm-up game, winning the contest by 7 wickets and plenty of balls to spare. Young Tanzid Hasan put on a stellar display before the likes of Litton Das and Mehidy Hasan capitalised on the fast start. Their bowling too looked solid and they will hope to cause an upset going into the main event. Who are you backing to win this one?
